# dsh-custom-mode
English | 中文
Edit your DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) assistants' system prompts, base modes and plugin switches. Keep
separate assistants for different tasks.
Install · First use · Updates · Screenshots · Compatibility · Help
## Editing and draft safety
This section describes editing and draft protection in `2.3.1`. Confirm that exact version is availa
ble in Releases before installing.
Select **New assistant…** in the page header to move to the existing creation form and focus its nam
e input. Creating the assistant still requires choosing its starting settings, naming it and submitt
ing the form. The currently selected assistant remains the editing target until creation succeeds. E
nter is ignored while text is being composed; ordinary Enter submits the completed name.
Drafts remain in memory for the **current browser document**, including when you leave and return to
the settings page. They are not a disk backup: reloading the document, closing the tab or restartin
g/unloading the plugin can lose unsaved edits. A leave-page warning cannot restore text after you co
nfirm leaving. Copy or export important draft text first. When duplicating with pending edits, confi
rm that the copy uses the saved configuration; the original draft is retained.
Restoring the starting prompt, importing a file or loading saved history replaces only the prompt dr
aft. If that would overwrite unsaved prompt text, confirm the replacement first; canceling keeps the
text. Saving is still required to write the files.
If a save reports a conflict, copy the complete draft before selecting **Discard edits and reload**.
A routine refresh keeps the dirty draft and its original baseline; it does not resolve the conflict
. Compare the newly loaded files with your copied text before applying the intended edits again.
## Install and make the first request
These instructions describe version `2.3.1`. Confirm that the exact version is available in Releases
, and check the exact-host results and acceptance limits before installing or updating.
Start with an installed DeepSeek Harness and a model configured through its own interface. Check `ds
h --version` against the exact hosts in the compatibility record. This package does not install the
host or configure model credentials.
### Web / CLI
Pin the plugin version; a bare name can resolve an older build during pnpm's release cooldown:

Restart the process that serves this Web profile using its usual launcher. For a local CLI instance,
the existing launch form is `dsh web --port 3081 --no-open`; use a free port and open the URL print
ed by that process. Restart only that instance. Installing a bundle does not refresh an already runn
t process. Restart only that instance. Installing a bundle does not refresh an already running host.
### Desktop and Windows
In the desktop app, use its **Plugins** page to install `dsh-custom-mode@2.3.1`, then restart the ap
p. This project's scripts deliberately refuse `--profile desktop`; do not modify its profile files b
y hand. Windows/Electron acceptance remains separate from Web acceptance; see the compatibility reco
and. Windows/Electron acceptance remains separate from Web acceptance; see the compatibility record.
On Windows, the npm installation above can use the host's `dsh` command from PowerShell. Only the op
tional clone installer requires Git Bash (plus Node.js and npm). If `dsh` is not on PATH, use the ho
st's supplied launcher, or replace `dsh` with `node "<host-install>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/li
b/bin.js"`. Do not point that path at this plugin's directory unless the host is actually installed
js"`. Do not point that path at this plugin's directory unless the host is actually installed there.
### Verify the whole path
1. Open Settings → Custom mode and check the displayed version. A page that opens is only the first

check.
2. Select **New assistant…** in the page header to focus the creation form. Choose a starting
setting such as Writing, enter a recognizable name and select New assistant. The created assistant

becomes the editing target.
[该节后续省略]
## What each choice means
The assistant selected on the settings page is the **one being edited**. Selecting or creating it do
es not change the assistant used by a new session. On first activation, the plugin may fill a missin
g default with the built-in `custom` assistant; an existing default is preserved. A newly created Wr
iting assistant still needs to be chosen in the session selector.
Choose the creation starting settings first; a new assistant starts from Standard. After creation, i
ts base mode and individual plugin switches can be adjusted in its editor.
| Starting settings | Initial behavior |

| Coding | Official Standard mode, tools as shipped. |
| Writing | Official Standard mode; terminal

off, file tools on. |
| Chat | Official Standard mode; files and terminal off. |
The prompt is stored in `prompt.md` and reread when the next model step is assembled. History and fi
le import load a draft; saving writes it. A stale save is refused when the underlying file changed.
`custom_prompt` asks for approval before it writes the same file. Turning off the Identity/persona r
ow also turns off this prompt's injection.
## Compatibility and versioning
The plugin version is its own stable `x.y.z` line; it does not mirror DSH. On 2026-11-04 the public
host tags were `latest=0.2.1-rc.5`, `next=0.2.2-rc.1`, and `alpha=0.2.2-alpha.3`. Tags move; the dec
lared range and completed checks are separate facts. See exact versions, acceptance limits and histo
rical evidence for the tested scope.
Release requires the compatibility and browser workflows. The unit runner, real prompt-component che
cks, packed-install checks and browser checks cover different boundaries. Windows/Electron, a real m
odel response and GPU execution must each have their own evidence; they are not inferred from a page
screenshot or unit count. Headless mode does not start an agent-preset session.
